candidates.exact_span: EPA-approved test procedures (methods) for the analysis and quantification of pollutants or pollutant parameters, including for the purposes of compliance monitoring/DMR reporting, permit renewal applications, or any other reporting that may be required as a condition of this permit, shall be sufficiently sensitive.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a method is 'sufficiently sensitive' governs whether reported analytical results are valid for compliance-limit comparison (A) and whether the method satisfies applicable compliance-monitoring/DMR reporting obligations (B).

candidates.exact_span: A method is "sufficiently sensitive" when (1) the method minimum level (ML) of quantification is at or below the level of the applicable effluent limit for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter; or (2) if there is no EPA-approved analytical method with a published ML at or below the effluent limit (see table below), then the method has the lowest published ML (is the most sensitive) of the analytical methods approved under 40 CFR Part 136 or required under 40 CFR Chapter I, Subchapters N or 0, for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter; or (3) the method is specified in this permit or has been otherwise approved in writing by the permitting authority (EPA Region 6) for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The three-part test links method quantification levels to applicable effluent limits and alternate approval pathways; different readings of which branch applies change whether a measurement can be compared to an enforceable limit (A) and whether the chosen method meets monitoring-method requirements (B).

candidates.exact_span: The Permittee has the option of developing and submitting a report to justify the use of matrix or sample-specific MLs rather than the published levels. Upon written approval by EPA Region 6 the matrix or sample-specific MLs may be utilized by the Permittee for all future Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) reporting requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether matrix or sample-specific MLs were approved in writing changes which quantification level governs sensitivity and reporting; that in turn can change limit-exceedance evaluation (A), whether monitoring/reporting used an acceptable method (B), and how below-quantification results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: Current EPA Region 6 minimum quantification levels (MQLs) for reporting and compliance are provided in Appendix A of Part II of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Appendix A supplies the operative MQL values used for reporting and compliance; uncertainty about which MQL applies to a parameter changes whether a reported value is treated as a valid numeric compliance comparison (A) and how sub-MQL results are interpreted (C).

candidates.computation_change_reason: This qualifier routes listed pollutants to the alternate 'lowest published ML' branch of the sensitivity test; different interpretations of membership in this list or what 'if specified' requires change applicable method-sensitivity rules (B) and whether a result can be compared to the effluent limit under branch (1) vs (2) (A).

candidates.exact_span: Unless otherwise indicated in this permit, if the EPA Region 6 MQL for a pollutant or pollutant parameter is sufficiently sensitive (as defined above) and the analytical test result is less than the MQL, then a value of zero (0) may be used for reporting purposes on DMRs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This rule determines when a sub-MQL analytical result may be reported as zero rather than as a detected value or non-reportable result; different readings change exceedance analysis against numeric limits (A) and whether missing/below-detection evidence is treated as documented zero, conditional non-requirement, or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: Furthermore, if the EPA Region 6 MQL for a pollutant or parameter is not sufficiently sensitive, but the analytical test result is less than the published ML from a sufficiently sensitive method, then a value of zero (0) may be used for reporting purposes on DMRs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This alternate zero-reporting pathway applies when the Region 6 MQL is not sufficiently sensitive; interpreting whether that condition is met and which published ML controls changes numeric compliance comparisons (A) and the established state for results without ordinary numeric reported values (C).
